claim: The KMK agreement of 10.03.1986 in the version of 15.06.2023 sets which IB subject combinations give German university entrance, and it is a subject rule rather than a points rule.
interpretation: This is the single most decision-relevant document in Europe for an IB student, and it is decided years before the application: it governs which six subjects you take, not how well you do in them. A student who takes the wrong combination cannot fix it with points, and cannot fix it at all after choosing. The document is a PDF, so nothing automated here can re-read it — it needs a person before each cycle, and the annexes carry their own separate revision dates.

claim: For medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy, applicants whose school-leaving certificate is dated after 15 January of the application year apply by 15 July; those with an earlier certificate apply by 31 May.
interpretation: An IB candidate receiving results in early July falls into the later group, so 15 July is their deadline and 31 May is not — but a student who took a gap year falls into the earlier group and 31 May is. Those two sentences decide the year for a would-be medic, and the distinction is invisible unless someone points it out. Dates recorded are the published 2026 ones; the 2027 dates are not yet published.
